findings.problem: The title asserts atomic commitment of the payment and notification. The changed function instead commits the database transaction before invoking external publication. Publication can then reject without delivering a notification while the payment remains committed, as the modeled publish-before case illustrates. The contract also permits a process stop between awaited operations without a durable outbox or background retry. The title repeats the author's unsupported atomicity claim and contradicts the supported body and recap.

evidence.quote: It fulfills with undefined after commit.
publish is an external operation outside the database transaction. Its rejection may happen before or after an externally visible notification.
A process can stop between awaited operations. No durable outbox, background retry, or cross-call lock is supplied.
The author says moving publish prevents notifications for failed commits and makes payment and notification atomic.
In-memory staged transaction and external notification counter; no actual database or process-kill simulation.

edits.value: Payment commits before notification, with a remaining delivery gap
